items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: But he was my favorite, Don was. He was such a fine guy.

ctx.x: Well, you know, Don would put them in those like what we say concert keys like E natural or B natural, working four, five sharps. So you get, [like you do the thing] -- like when a fellow come in town, just say, well, just start with C, play in the key of C and keep on going. See how long they'd last. (Unintelligible).

items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: That's Fat Man's home too, Charleston, West Virginia.

ctx.x: He says, what do you play? I said, the saxophone. I remember Chu first came to New York. Said, what are you drinking? I said, a little gin and anisette. He said, you don't pay for nothing in here. That's the way it was. He was just loved. And that's Fat Man's home too, Charleston, West Virginia.
Did he come up with him? Did they come up together? I forget.

items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Don really was exacting. [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, he was. He finished that Virginia State University.

ctx.x: Yes, he was. He finished that Virginia State University. He finished down there in music, you know, and he could play -- I think the ocarina was a little, funny instrument.
